changelog: Replace C1 to prioritize single high-contradiction boundaries: explicitly tell scorers to rank cuts that would be contradicted by the remainder below other cuts, addressing the primary_finding.

Insert a new principle after C3 that warns against cutting right after auxiliaries/copulas/modals/negators/subordinators when the remainder completes or reverses the predicate, phrased as a ranking preference to avoid blanket bans.
Paraphrase C4 shorter to save space while keeping its guidance about noun+modifier splits and avoiding forcing tiny fragments.
findings: The prompt underrates single high-contradiction boundaries: it lets one cut with a high contradiction risk survive because cohesion looks OK, even though one such boundary can zero the whole set.

The prompt fails to flag cuts that isolate unresolved function‑headed predicates: it allows cutting immediately after an auxiliary/copula/modal/negation/subordinator, leaving the remainder to complete or flip the predicate.

diagnosis.why: The C1 change (prioritizing boundaries whose remainder would contradict the prefix) made the scorer avoid cuts that leave a contradicting remainder, which raised scores on long pieces; the new C3 warning about cutting after auxiliaries/copulas/modals shifted many cuts away from those markers into adjacent short spans, increasing harmful short-latency splits (bins ≤3 and ≤5) and producing the small net drop.
diagnosis.lesson: Keep the preference to demote single high-contradiction boundaries (C1) but avoid re-ranking that pushes cuts into head-adjacent tiny spans (subject/auxiliary splits or noun+modifier fragments) that damage very short latency bins.
